source.label: Wikipedia: Zhao’s own inscription is one of five blocks of text in the sky

highlight.text: Five blocks of Chinese text are written in the sky above the scene. One of these is by Zhao himself and includes his signature. The remainder are notes added much later by the 18th-century Qianlong Emperor of the Qing dynasty.

work.text: Reinforcing the idyllic nature of the piece, Zhao painted it in a deliberately archaic style. His use of texture patterns is similar to that of the 10th century artists Dong Yuan and Juran, while the twisted tree trunks recall those of Li Cheng. However, unlike the dramatic and monumental landscape paintings of that period, it depicts a relatively simple and quiet scene.

moment.text: The painting attracted widespread acclaim from later Chinese artists and scholars. Many imitation pieces have been made after Zhao's original over the following seven centuries.
